entry.title: More ways to leave a mark
entry.summary: Davies offers chalk and paint as ways to explore movement and materials, with adult help and supervision. A finished picture is not the aim.
entry.cue: A child who enjoys marks may become interested in a brush, chalk, or a larger surface.
detail: Her watercolor example begins with one color, a brush, a small water jar, paper on an underlay, and a spill cloth. The child explores wetting the brush, picking up paint, and moving it on paper.

Chalk on a large board or sidewalk gives room for whole-arm movement and wiping with an eraser. For easel painting, her table specifies standing unaided, a short-handled chunky brush, and one color of thick paint in a cup.
Davies suggests putting paint out for younger toddlers when an adult can supervise. As with drawing, she shows how to use a material and leaves the experiment to the child.
